title: Keeping AI NPC systems organized is becoming a bigger challenge than building them
author: Resilienceest_581
selftext:
I'm working on a small AI game prototype where different agents handle dialogue, quests, NPC memory, and a few world events. The AI part has actually been easier than I expected.

The messy part is keeping all those workflows connected without breaking something every time I make a change. After a while I stopped worrying about prompts and started worrying about my own project structure.

I've been testing a few different ways to organize everything. So far it's been useful for seeing how the agents interact instead of jumping between a bunch of separate scripts and notes. I'm still figuring out whether I'll stick with that approach or move everything back into code later.

How are you organizing multi agent systems once a project starts getting bigger? Are you using visual workflows, or are you keeping everything in code?

comments.author: tschilpi
comments.body:
There is no way around proper systems engineering, e.g. keeping systems decoupled and modular, understanding their seams, and how they interact with each other.  
It helps to isolate issues and let agents work on them. Have a couple regression and integration tests. Keep working on the architecture and making small improvements over time. Try to reduce complexity and overengineering. Etc.

comments.author: Commercial-Egg4672
comments.body: AI is still evolving, and manual intervention is often required; [triverse.ai](http://triverse.ai) is currently free, and its basic features are sufficient.
